ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Each face of two noncongruent parallelepipeds is a rhombus whose diagonals have lengths $\sqrt{21}$ and $\sqrt{31}$. The ratio of the volume of the larger of the two polyhedra to the volume of the smaller is $\fracmn$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers. Find $m+n$. A parallelepiped is a solid with six parallelogram faces such as the one shown below.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a tilted parallelepiped, with dashed lines indicating the obscured edges. It can be regarded as being generated by three edge vectors a, b, c starting from the same vertex, and all six faces are parallelograms; the problem states that these faces are all rhombi. Reasoning: Let the three adjacent edge vectors be a, b, c. Each face is a rhombus, and the two diagonal lengths of the rhombus are respectively √21 and √31. For a rhombus formed by two equal-length side vectors u, v, the side length squared satisfies |u|^2 = |v|^2 = (21+31)/4 = 13, so |a|^2 = |b|^2 = |c|^2 = 13. The two diagonals on the same face correspond to u+v and u−v, so |u+v|^2 and |u−v|^2 are respectively 31 and 21. Since |u+v|^2 = 26 + 2u·v and |u−v|^2 = 26 − 2u·v, it follows that the dot product of each pair of adjacent edge vectors is ±5/2. Thus the diagonal entries of the Gram matrix G are 13, and the three off-diagonal dot products x = a·b, y = b·c, z = c·a are all ±5/2. The volume squared is det(G), namely V^2 = 13^3 − 13(x^2+y^2+z^2) + 2xyz. Since x^2+y^2+z^2 = 3·25/4, the common part is 13^3 − 13·3·25/4 = 2197 − 975/4 = 7813/4. The two non-congruent cases are distinguished by the sign of xyz. If xyz > 0, then 2xyz = 2(5/2)^3 = 125/4, so V^2 = 7813/4 + 125/4 = 3969/2. If xyz < 0, then V^2 = 7813/4 − 125/4 = 1922. The ratio of the larger volume to the smaller volume is sqrt((3969/2)/1922) = sqrt(3969/3844) = 63/62. Therefore m = 63, n = 62, and m+n = 125.

method.method_draft: Use a vector/Gram-matrix model of the parallelepiped. From the diagram, treat the solid as generated by three edge vectors \(\mathbf a,\mathbf b,\mathbf c\) meeting at one vertex. From the text, each face is a rhombus with diagonals \(\sqrt{21}\) and \(\sqrt{31}\). For a rhombus face spanned by two edge vectors, \(|\mathbf a|^2=(21+31)/4=13\), so all three edge vectors have squared length 13. Also \(|\mathbf a+\mathbf b|^2\) and \(|\mathbf a-\mathbf b|^2\) are 31 and 21, so each pairwise dot product is \(\pm 5/2\). Thus the Gram matrix has diagonal entries 13 and off-diagonal entries \(\pm 5/2\). The two noncongruent cases are distinguished by the sign of the product of the three off-diagonal entries. Compute \(V^2=\det G=13^3-13\cdot 3\cdot(25/4)+2(\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf b)(\mathbf b\cdot\mathbf c)(\mathbf c\cdot\mathbf a)\), giving \(3969/2\) and \(1922\). Therefore the volume ratio is \(\sqrt{(3969/2)/1922}=63/62\), so \(m+n=125\).

图像描述：图中画的是一个倾斜的平行六面体，虚线表示被遮挡的棱。它可以看作由同一顶点出发的三条棱向量 a, b, c 生成，六个面都是平行四边形；题目说明这些面都是菱形。

推理：设三条相邻棱向量为 a, b, c。每个面是菱形，且菱形两条对角线长分别为 √21 和 √31。对于由两个等长边向量 u, v 形成的菱形，边长平方满足 |u|^2 = |v|^2 = (21+31)/4 = 13，所以 |a|^2 = |b|^2 = |c|^2 = 13。

同一面上的两条对角线对应 u+v 和 u−v，因此 |u+v|^2 与 |u−v|^2 分别是 31 和 21。由于 |u+v|^2 = 26 + 2u·v，|u−v|^2 = 26 − 2u·v，可得每一对相邻棱向量的点积都是 ±5/2。

于是 Gram 矩阵 G 的对角元为 13，三个非对角点积 x = a·b, y = b·c, z = c·a 都是 ±5/2。体积平方为 det(G)，即 V^2 = 13^3 − 13(x^2+y^2+z^2) + 2xyz。因为 x^2+y^2+z^2 = 3·25/4，所以公共部分为 13^3 − 13·3·25/4 = 2197 − 975/4 = 7813/4。

两个非全等情形由 xyz 的符号区分。若 xyz > 0，则 2xyz = 2(5/2)^3 = 125/4，所以 V^2 = 7813/4 + 125/4 = 3969/2。若 xyz < 0，则 V^2 = 7813/4 − 125/4 = 1922。

较大体积与较小体积的比为 sqrt((3969/2)/1922) = sqrt(3969/3844) = 63/62。因此 m = 63, n = 62，m+n = 125。

method.method_draft: Convert the parallelepiped into an auxiliary tetrahedron. From the diagram, choose four alternating vertices of the parallelepiped, for example \(O,\mathbf a+\mathbf b,\mathbf a+\mathbf c,\mathbf b+\mathbf c\). The six edges of this tetrahedron are exactly face diagonals of the parallelepiped, so by the text each has length \(\sqrt{21}\) or \(\sqrt{31}\). Opposite edges come from the two diagonals of the same rhombus face, so each opposite pair consists of one \(\sqrt{21}\) edge and one \(\sqrt{31}\) edge. The two possible noncongruent arrangements are equivalent to tetrahedra with an equilateral base of side \(\sqrt{21}\) and three equal lateral edges \(\sqrt{31}\), or an equilateral base of side \(\sqrt{31}\) and three equal lateral edges \(\sqrt{21}\). For an equilateral-base tetrahedron with base side \(b\) and lateral edge \(l\), \(V_T^2=b^4(3l^2-b^2)/144\). This gives tetrahedron volume squares \(441/2\) and \(1922/9\). The chosen tetrahedron has one-third the parallelepiped volume, so the parallelepiped volume squares are \(3969/2\) and \(1922\). The ratio is \(63/62\), hence \(m+n=125\).

Image description: The attached figures show generic slanted parallelepipeds drawn in perspective, with solid visible edges and dotted hidden edges. They serve as diagrams of the parallelepiped shape; no extra numerical labels are shown.

Reasoning: Let the three edge vectors of a parallelepiped be a, b, and c from a common vertex O. Following the assigned method, choose the four alternating vertices O, a+b, a+c, and b+c. These form an auxiliary tetrahedron. Its six edges are vectors a+b, a+c, b+c, b-a, c-a, and c-b, which are exactly diagonals of the rhombus faces of the original parallelepiped. Therefore every tetrahedron edge has length sqrt(21) or sqrt(31). Also, opposite edges of this tetrahedron come from the two diagonals of the same rhombus face, so each opposite pair contains one edge of length sqrt(21) and one edge of length sqrt(31).

The two possible noncongruent arrangements are equivalent to tetrahedra with an equilateral base of side sqrt(21) and three equal lateral edges sqrt(31), or an equilateral base of side sqrt(31) and three equal lateral edges sqrt(21).

For an equilateral-base tetrahedron with base side b and lateral edge l, the base area is (sqrt(3)/4)b^2, and the height satisfies h^2 = l^2 - b^2/3. Thus V_T^2 = (1/9)(3b^4/16)(l^2 - b^2/3) = b^4(3l^2-b^2)/144.

Case 1: b = sqrt(21), l = sqrt(31). Then V_T^2 = 21^2(3*31-21)/144 = 441*72/144 = 441/2.

Case 2: b = sqrt(31), l = sqrt(21). Then V_T^2 = 31^2(3*21-31)/144 = 961*32/144 = 1922/9.

The chosen tetrahedron has one-third the volume of the original parallelepiped, so the parallelepiped volume squares are 9*(441/2) = 3969/2 and 9*(1922/9) = 1922.

The ratio of the larger volume to the smaller volume is sqrt((3969/2)/1922) = sqrt(3969/3844) = 63/62. Hence m+n = 63+62 = 125.

The two diagonals on the same face correspond to u+v and u−v, so |u+v|^2 and |u−v|^2 are respectively 31 and 21. Since |u+v|^2 = 26 + 2u·v and |u−v|^2 = 26 − 2u·v, it follows that the dot product of each pair of adjacent edge vectors is ±5/2.

Thus the diagonal entries of the Gram matrix G are 13, and the three off-diagonal dot products x = a·b, y = b·c, z = c·a are all ±5/2. The volume squared is det(G), namely V^2 = 13^3 − 13(x^2+y^2+z^2) + 2xyz. Since x^2+y^2+z^2 = 3·25/4, the common part is 13^3 − 13·3·25/4 = 2197 − 975/4 = 7813/4.

The two non-congruent cases are distinguished by the sign of xyz. If xyz > 0, then 2xyz = 2(5/2)^3 = 125/4, so V^2 = 7813/4 + 125/4 = 3969/2. If xyz < 0, then V^2 = 7813/4 − 125/4 = 1922.

The ratio of the larger volume to the smaller volume is sqrt((3969/2)/1922) = sqrt(3969/3844) = 63/62. Therefore m = 63, n = 62, and m+n = 125.
